director.chapterArc: A siege begins on a raised embankment (the Level). Rook's physical capacity has collapsed to 'a tenth,' leaving him unable to fight or hold barriers effectively. The group is ambushed by twenty-two men who use psychological warfare (nine stationary fires) and tactical flanking via water reeds. A brief skirmish results in three casualties but fails to stop the main force, leading Rook to be stabbed by a non-combatant. The chapter ends with the group establishing a night-time hold on a narrow spur behind an engine house as new moon approaches.
director.restraintNote: Maintain Toren's sensory proximity without adopting his teenage voice; the narrator is older, cooler, and more observant than the protagonist. Differentiate characters by status, rhythm, reserve, and conversational pressure rather than accent or caricature. Avoid 'wonder' tones for magical elements; treat them as physical tools with mechanical costs.

cues.delivery: Rook's tactical briefing on the nine fires. Economical, flat affect. Low register with high authority conveyed through silence and precision.
cues.from: "No," said Rook. "And none of them have been fed, and none of them have gone down, and a fire a man's sitting at does both. Those are nine fires built to be counted. He told you a day and a half and then he lit you nine fires and went to bed, and the four of you have been standing up in the dark ever since watching them very carefully.
cues.through: "I'm at a tenth and I'm not going to be at a fifth in the morning whatever anybody does, and you four are going to be worth exactly what you've slept." He sat down on the cart shaft. "That's the first thing a company does and it doesn't cost them a thing. They can't get at you for a day so they spend the day making you tired, and the reason it works is that being frightened feels like doing something. Boots off."
cues.reason: Establishes Rook as a leader who is physically failing but mentally sharp.

cues.delivery: Dessa's report. Quiet intensity. Low, direct voice avoiding pity.
cues.from: Dessa woke them before light with one word.
cues.through: "Six," said Dessa. "They've been coming up the slope out of the water in ones since about the fourth hour. That's eight north of us and they're all on the far side of the sluice and I can't get any further than thirty feet, so there might be twelve, and I'd rather say eight and be honest than say twelve and be useful."
cues.reason: Shifts focus to the immediate threat; Dessa is the group's sensor.

cues.delivery: Rook confirms the trap and issues orders. Commands are statements, not questions with rising inflection.
cues.from: "Was never on offer," said Rook. "It was on offer if I walked out, and it wasn't on offer then either, and the reason I know that is that he put eight men across it four hours after he said it." He looked at Toren, briefly. "That's the register. That's the whole of what I've been trying to teach you since the field with the sleeping places in it. Everything he said to us last night was true, including the bit about the wheel, and none of it was going to happen."
cues.through: "Senna stays in the bed and doesn't sit up," said Rook, "and if she sits up I'll say something I can't take back."
cues.reason: The tactical pivot from 'negotiation' to 'combat'. Rook is exhausted but decisive.

cues.delivery: Toren's internal observation of the enemy. Analytical rhythm.
cues.from: "Left hump, near end, low," said Toren, and his voice came out about a third of the size he had sent it.
cues.reason: First contact; Toren is observing human behavior rather than fighting.

cues.delivery: The fight begins. Staccato, fragmented sentences during combat or panic (Toren's internal monologue). Describe violence clinically.
cues.from: Wyck Tanner stepped one pace forward into the middle of the road and planted.
cues.through: That was the part nobody had prepared him for and there was no preparing anybody for it. A husk resisted. A husk was a sack of wrong meat and you had to shove. This went in the way a knife goes into a cheese, and the man's whole weight came onto it and then off it, and he sat down in the road with his leg out in front of him making a high sound with no words in it at all, and his hatchet was on the ground three feet away and neither of them looked at it.
cues.reason: Action sequence; focus on physical sensation and immediate consequence.

cues.delivery: The enemy retreats. Rook's voice is flat; Toren's realization of the trap.
cues.through: The whistle was for the water.
cues.reason: Transition from combat to tactical re-evaluation.

cues.delivery: Milo's light trap. Milo is white-lipped but grinning; dissociation.
cues.from: "Nine," she called. "Nine in the water and they're at the bank now. Now, Rook—"
cues.through: "They shot at it," said Milo. He was white to the lips and he was grinning, which was a thing his face did when it had nowhere else to go. "They shot at it twice. It's in the road. It's in the road, it's not in my hands, I did the thing—"
cues.reason: The boy with the light becomes a target; Toren observes the horror of his utility.

cues.delivery: The siege begins. Rook's explanation of enemy psychology.
cues.from: Toren had been in four fights and all of them had been a short violent confusion that arrived, and emptied him, and was over, and left ash on the grass to be lifted. This was an hour long. It had stretches in it where nothing happened at all, where he stood on the crown of a brick arch with his heart going and his arm aching and watched men two hundred feet away doing sensible unhurried things: dragging a boat up, sitting down, changing a wet boot, arguing.
cues.through: The second time they came at the water side, four of them up the bank slope onto the spur below the engine house where the ground was flat, and that was Dessa's, entirely. She called them out of the reeds one at a time while they were still crawling — "One at the sluice head, he's low, he's at the third gate — two more behind him on the stone — the far one's stopped, he's stopped, he's waiting for the other two" — and Rook went down the inside of the bank and met the first man at the sluice head before the man had got his feet under him, and that was the end of that, and it was fast and it was ugly and Toren, above on the arch, made himself watch it and wished, watching it, that he hadn't.
cues.reason: Rook is teaching Toren about human fear vs. physical threat.

cues.delivery: Rook's injury. Clinical description of the wound; Rook is in pain but mentally sharp.
cues.from: The fourth time they got Rook.
cues.through: It was the thing he could not get past that whole grey morning, and afterward he thought it was probably the moment he stopped being able to think about the two kinds of fighting as one subject with two chapters in it. There was a man in the road twenty feet from him with a spear in him. There was blood on the brickwork of the arch in a long smear where Wyck had come off it. There was a boot. There was a cap.
cues.reason: The turning point where Rook loses his physical edge.

cues.delivery: Rook's debrief. He is bleeding but focused on the arithmetic of survival.
cues.from: "Don't," said Rook, beside him, without looking.
cues.through: "Not on myself. You can't get the angle." He got his coat closed one-handed. "It doesn't matter. What matters is the arithmetic and I'll give it you now and then I'd like an hour.
cues.reason: The shift from fighting to planning a siege.

cues.delivery: Rook declares Milo the most important person. Quiet intensity.
cues.from: "That's a siege," said Wyck. "You said a held place is a grave."
cues.through: "Which makes the boy with the light the most important person on this bank," he said, "and everybody here is going to have to live with that, including him."
cues.reason: The emotional weight of the chapter's conclusion.

pauses.after: "No," said Rook. "And none of them have been fed, and none of them have gone down, and a fire a man's sitting at does both. Those are nine fires built to be counted. He told you a day and a half and then he lit you nine fires and went to bed, and the four of you have been standing up in the dark ever since watching them very carefully.
pauses.reason: Completed thought on the nine fires; let the tactical reality land.

pauses.after: "North," she said. "Across the arch. Two on the road bed at twenty-eight, and something on the water side of the bank below them that isn't standing up. They came past me while it was still dark and I had them and I let them, because there was nothing to be done about two men at four in the morning and I wanted to know if there'd be more."
pauses.reason: Speaker reset after Dessa's report; transition to Rook's analysis.

pauses.after: "Was never on offer," said Rook. "It was on offer if I walked out, and it wasn't on offer then either, and the reason I know that is that he put eight men across it four hours after he said it." He looked at Toren, briefly. "That's the register. That's the whole of what I've been trying to teach you since the field with the sleeping places in it. Everything he said to us last night was true, including the bit about the wheel, and none of it was going to happen."
pauses.reason: Completed thought on the trap being sprung; pause for Toren's realization.

pauses.after: Something down there swore, and stood up, and a voice back in the dark said "Hold—" and another voice, further off, said "Now," at the same instant, and Toren learned in that half second the single thing about human beings that a hundred husks had never taught him: they disagreed. Two men on the same side, twenty feet apart, with two different ideas about the next second, and both ideas happened.
pauses.reason: Major emotional landing: The revelation that humans disagree. Let this sink in before action starts.
Emphasis on the fundamental difference between human and non-human threats.
Completed thought on the ease of killing a human; pause for Toren's internal shock.
Isolating the shocking ease of killing a man compared to fighting husks.

pauses.after: "Nine," she called. "Nine in the water and they're at the bank now. Now, Rook—"
pauses.reason: Dessa calls out 'Nine'; brief pause before Rook confirms her count.
Emphasis on the number; Dessa's count is critical and counter-intuitive.

pauses.after: "Yes," said Rook, going past him. "Pick it up and put it out. It's daylight and you've spent it."
pauses.reason: Rook's command to Milo; let the order land as a tactical necessity.

pauses.after: Pitch, who had been through a road cut and a bridge in fog and an orchard in the dark, and who had a low and entirely accurate opinion of people, put his head down and hit the man with his shoulder and stood on his foot, and the man went off the bank backward, and Milo laughed with his whole body for about four seconds and then stopped and sat down on the road and put his hands over his face.
pauses.reason: Milo laughs then stops. A beat of silence for his reaction to the violence.

pauses.before: Milo laughed with his whole body
pauses.reason: Isolating Milo's reaction to the absurdity of the situation; highlights his dissociation.

pauses.after: "You were about to work out what that's worth," said Rook. "It isn't worth anything. It's a man in a road and the ground keeps him. That's the whole difference and you'll spend the rest of your life on it and I can't shorten it for you."
pauses.reason: Rook's lesson on human flesh vs. husks; pause for Toren to process the difference.
Emphasis on Rook's harsh truth about human bodies and blood.

pauses.after: "We are not going north. The block will be back on that road before dark and there'll be more of it. We are not going south. So we go onto the spur, behind the brick, and we put the cart where the ground is narrow, and we hold a piece of bank thirty feet wide, and that is not a plan, it is what is left."
pauses.reason: Speaker reset after Rook outlines the siege plan; transition to Wyck's objection.
Emphasis on Milo's new role; a heavy realization for the group and Toren.
